blocks.en: 1. Gathering the Witnesses
blocks.es_reference: 1. Reuniendo a los Testigos

blocks.en: We asked, at the very beginning of this course, a plain and pressing question: can we trust the Bible we hold in our hands? We refused to answer it with a skeptic's easy sneer or a salesman's easy boast. Instead we called four witnesses, and we made each of them testify under honest examination. The first witness, the canon, gave us the right books — recognized by the church, not invented by it. The second witness, the text, gave us the right words — kept for us in such an abundance of manuscripts that no honest doubt can erase them; the same Word stands in your New King James and your Reina-Valera that the church has always held. The third witness, archaeology, showed us the real events — the world of the Bible lifted out of the ground and correlated, name upon name. The fourth witness, geography, showed us the real stage — a land so exactly known that you may walk the Bible with a map in your hand. Four witnesses have spoken; four testimonies lie before us. It remains now to ask the final question: what do they say when we hear them together?
blocks.es_reference: Preguntamos, al mismísimo principio de este curso, una pregunta sencilla y apremiante: ¿podemos confiar en la Biblia que tenemos en nuestras manos? Nos negamos a responderla con la burla fácil de un escéptico o la jactancia fácil de un vendedor. En cambio llamamos a cuatro testigos, e hicimos que cada uno de ellos testificara bajo examen honesto. El primer testigo, el canon, nos dio los libros correctos — reconocidos por la iglesia, no inventados por ella. El segundo testigo, el texto, nos dio las palabras correctas — guardadas para nosotros en tal abundancia de manuscritos que ninguna duda honesta puede borrarlas; la misma Palabra está en tu Nueva King James y tu Reina-Valera que la iglesia siempre ha sostenido. El tercer testigo, la arqueología, nos mostró los eventos reales — el mundo de la Biblia levantado de la tierra y correlacionado, nombre tras nombre. El cuarto testigo, la geografía, nos mostró el escenario real — una tierra tan exactamente conocida que puedes caminar la Biblia con un mapa en la mano. Cuatro testigos han hablado; cuatro testimonios yacen ante nosotros. Queda ahora hacer la pregunta final: ¿qué dicen cuando los oímos juntos?

blocks.en: 2. How a Cumulative Case Works
blocks.es_reference: 2. Cómo Funciona un Caso Acumulativo

blocks.en: No single witness proves the Bible; we have said so at every step — correlation, not proof. But witnesses do not testify one at a time in sealed rooms; they testify together, and their agreement carries a force that no one of them has alone. In a court of law, a single thread may be explained away, but a hundred threads woven together make a rope that holds a great weight. So it is here. That the books are the right ones; that the words have been faithfully kept; that the events are grounded in real soil; that the stage is a real and knowable land — each of these, by itself, is a single strand. But braid them together, and they make an overwhelming case that this book is exactly what it claims to be: a true record, rooted in real history, faithfully handed down to us. The strength of the whole is not the mere sum of its parts; it is far greater than the sum. This is how honest confidence is built — never by one dramatic knockout proof, but by the quiet convergence of many independent witnesses, all pointing the same way.
blocks.es_reference: Ningún testigo por sí solo prueba la Biblia; lo hemos dicho en cada paso — correlación, no prueba. Pero los testigos no testifican de uno en uno en cuartos sellados; testifican juntos, y su acuerdo lleva una fuerza que ninguno de ellos tiene solo. En un tribunal de justicia, un solo hilo puede explicarse, pero cien hilos tejidos juntos hacen una cuerda que sostiene un gran peso. Así es aquí. Que los libros son los correctos; que las palabras han sido fielmente guardadas; que los eventos están arraigados en tierra real; que el escenario es una tierra real y conocible — cada uno de estos, por sí mismo, es una sola hebra. Pero trénzalos juntos, y hacen un caso abrumador de que este libro es exactamente lo que afirma ser: un registro verdadero, arraigado en la historia real, fielmente transmitido a nosotros. La fuerza del todo no es la mera suma de sus partes; es mucho mayor que la suma. Así se construye la confianza honesta — nunca por una dramática prueba de golpe único, sino por la callada convergencia de muchos testigos independientes, todos apuntando en la misma dirección.

blocks.en: 3. Back to Luke's Purpose: "That You May Know the Certainty"
blocks.es_reference: 3. De Vuelta al Propósito de Lucas: "Para que Conozcas la Certeza"

blocks.en: Return now to the very words with which this course began — the opening of the Gospel of Luke. Luke tells Theophilus that many had undertaken to write of these things; that he himself had carefully investigated everything from the first, following those who were eyewitnesses and ministers of the word; and that he had set it all down in an orderly account. And then he tells him why he did it: "that you may know the certainty of those things in which you were instructed" (Luke 1:4). Mark that one word well: certainty. Luke did not labor over his investigation merely to give Theophilus a pleasant story or a warm feeling. He wrote so that Theophilus would know — know with certainty — that the things he had been taught were true and could be trusted. That was the whole purpose of the inquiry. And it has been the whole purpose of this course. We have done, in our own small and careful way, exactly what Luke invites every reader to do: we have examined the books, the words, the events, and the land. And so we may say to every Theophilus who holds a Bible today: you may know the certainty.
blocks.es_reference: Vuelve ahora a las mismísimas palabras con que este curso comenzó — el comienzo del Evangelio de Lucas. Lucas le dice a Teófilo que muchos habían intentado escribir de estas cosas; que él mismo había investigado cuidadosamente todo desde el principio, siguiendo a los que fueron testigos oculares y ministros de la palabra; y que lo había puesto todo por escrito en un relato ordenado. Y luego le dice por qué lo hizo: "para que conozcas bien la verdad de las cosas en las cuales has sido instruido" (es decir, la certeza) (Lucas 1:4). Marca bien esa palabra: certeza. Lucas no se afanó en su investigación meramente para darle a Teófilo una historia agradable o un sentimiento cálido. Escribió para que Teófilo conociera — conociera con certeza — que las cosas que le habían sido enseñadas eran verdaderas y podían ser confiadas. Ese fue todo el propósito de la indagación. Y ha sido todo el propósito de este curso. Hemos hecho, a nuestra propia manera pequeña y cuidadosa, exactamente lo que Lucas invita a hacer a todo lector: hemos examinado los libros, las palabras, los eventos y la tierra. Y así podemos decir a todo Teófilo que hoy tiene una Biblia: puedes conocer la certeza.

blocks.en: 4. Where Certainty Really Rests
blocks.es_reference: 4. Dónde Descansa Realmente la Certeza

blocks.en: But here we must be careful and clear, or we will build our house upon the sand. We have gathered a mighty cumulative case. Does our certainty, then, finally rest upon that case? No — and this is the very heart of the matter. The evidence is precious, but it is the servant, and not the master. If your certainty rested upon archaeology, it would rise and fall with the next spade turned in the next field; if it rested on a count of manuscripts, a cleverer skeptic might one day trouble it. A certainty that can be argued up can also be argued down. The true ground of certainty lies far deeper: it is that God Himself breathed out this Scripture, and that His Spirit bears witness in the heart of the believer that this is indeed His Word. The evidence does not create that certainty. What the evidence does is clear away the obstacles to it, and confirm it, and silence forever the false charge that faith is blind. The four witnesses strip away every reasonable excuse for doubting that the Bible can be trusted — but the certainty they serve rests upon the unchanging character of the God who spoke. Evidence is the servant of faith; it is never its foundation.
blocks.es_reference: Pero aquí debemos ser cuidadosos y claros, o edificaremos nuestra casa sobre la arena. Hemos reunido un poderoso caso acumulativo. ¿Descansa entonces nuestra certeza, finalmente, sobre ese caso? No — y este es el mismísimo corazón del asunto. La evidencia es preciosa, pero es la sierva, y no la señora. Si tu certeza descansara sobre la arqueología, subiría y caería con la próxima pala clavada en el próximo campo; si descansara sobre un conteo de manuscritos, un escéptico más astuto podría un día perturbarla. Una certeza que puede argumentarse a favor también puede argumentarse en contra. El verdadero fundamento de la certeza yace mucho más profundo: es que Dios mismo exhaló esta Escritura, y que su Espíritu da testimonio en el corazón del creyente de que esta es en verdad su Palabra. La evidencia no crea esa certeza. Lo que la evidencia hace es despejar los obstáculos a ella, y confirmarla, y silenciar para siempre la falsa acusación de que la fe es ciega. Los cuatro testigos quitan toda excusa razonable para dudar de que la Biblia puede ser confiada — pero la certeza a la que sirven descansa sobre el carácter inmutable del Dios que habló. La evidencia es la sierva de la fe; nunca es su fundamento.

blocks.en: 5. The Authority That Travels into Your Hands
blocks.es_reference: 5. La Autoridad que Desciende a Tus Manos

blocks.en: The Word of God is not a fortress you must defend inch by inch; it is a throne from which God speaks.
blocks.es_reference: La Palabra de Dios no es una fortaleza que debas defender palmo a palmo; es un trono desde el cual Dios habla.

blocks.en: And now we may say the thing this whole course has been moving toward from the first page. Because God gave His Word, and because God has faithfully kept His Word, the Bible you hold in your hands carries the full and absolute authority of God Himself. Notice carefully what we are saying, and what we are not. We are not saying that you must first prove every word before you are permitted to trust it; you cannot do that, and, thank God, you do not need to. Nor are we resting this authority upon the lost original manuscripts, as though the Word of God were locked away in autographs that no living soul has ever seen. We are saying that the authority of God travels down — through faithful copying, and through faithful translation — into the very Bible that lies open in your hands. When the apostles preached, they preached from copies and from translations, and they preached with the full authority of God. So may you. The Word of God is not a fortress you must anxiously defend inch by inch; it is a throne, from which God Himself speaks — and He speaks, with full and absolute authority, in the very book you are holding right now.
blocks.es_reference: Y ahora podemos decir aquello hacia lo cual todo este curso se ha estado moviendo desde la primera página. Porque Dios dio su Palabra, y porque Dios ha guardado fielmente su Palabra, la Biblia que tienes en tus manos lleva la plena y absoluta autoridad de Dios mismo. Nota cuidadosamente lo que estamos diciendo, y lo que no. No estamos diciendo que debas primero probar cada palabra antes de que se te permita confiar en ella; no puedes hacer eso, y, gracias a Dios, no necesitas hacerlo. Tampoco estamos descansando esta autoridad sobre los manuscritos originales perdidos, como si la Palabra de Dios estuviera encerrada en autógrafos que ningún alma viviente ha visto jamás. Estamos diciendo que la autoridad de Dios desciende — a través de la copia fiel, y a través de la traducción fiel — hasta la mismísima Biblia que yace abierta en tus manos. Cuando los apóstoles predicaban, predicaban de copias y de traducciones, y predicaban con la plena autoridad de Dios. Así puedes tú. La Palabra de Dios no es una fortaleza que debas defender ansiosamente palmo a palmo; es un trono, desde el cual Dios mismo habla — y habla, con plena y absoluta autoridad, en el mismísimo libro que estás sosteniendo ahora mismo.

blocks.en: 6. A Word to the Man in the Pew
blocks.es_reference: 6. Una Palabra para el Hombre en la Banca

blocks.en: Let us now speak very plainly, to the ordinary believer in the ordinary pew, who has followed this whole course and may still be quietly wondering. You do not hold the original page that Moses or Paul wrote; no one on earth does. You hold a translation — an English New King James, a Spanish Reina-Valera — of a copy of a copy. And we will not pretend otherwise; we have been honest about that from the very first unit. But now hear the promise, and hear it rightly. God never promised to place the autograph in your hands; He promised to preserve His Word. And He has done precisely that — so faithfully, so richly, across so many hands and so many centuries, that the Bible lying open before you tonight is the preserved and authoritative Word of God. You are not holding a faint and distant echo of God's Word; you are holding God's Word. So read it as such. Believe it as such. Obey it as such. The certainty that Luke wrote his Gospel to give is not reserved for scholars in their studies; it is for you — in your own language, in your own hands, this very night.
blocks.es_reference: Hablemos ahora muy claramente, al creyente común en la banca común, que ha seguido todo este curso y quizás aún se pregunta calladamente. No tienes la página original que Moisés o Pablo escribió; nadie en la tierra la tiene. Tienes una traducción — una Nueva King James en inglés, una Reina-Valera en español — de una copia de una copia. Y no fingiremos lo contrario; hemos sido honestos en eso desde la primerísima unidad. Pero ahora escucha la promesa, y escúchala correctamente. Dios nunca prometió poner el autógrafo en tus manos; prometió preservar su Palabra. Y ha hecho precisamente eso — tan fielmente, tan ricamente, a través de tantas manos y tantos siglos, que la Biblia que yace abierta ante ti esta noche es la Palabra preservada y autoritativa de Dios. No estás sosteniendo un eco débil y distante de la Palabra de Dios; estás sosteniendo la Palabra de Dios. Así que léela como tal. Créela como tal. Obedécela como tal. La certeza que Lucas escribió su Evangelio para dar no está reservada para los eruditos en sus estudios; es para ti — en tu propia lengua, en tus propias manos, esta misma noche.

blocks.en: 7. The Fruit of Honest Confidence
blocks.es_reference: 7. El Fruto de la Confianza Honesta

blocks.en: Not a nervous certainty that fears the next question, but a settled certainty that has faced the questions and stands.
blocks.es_reference: No una certeza nerviosa que teme la próxima pregunta, sino una certeza asentada que ha enfrentado las preguntas y se mantiene.

blocks.en: See now why we took the harder road — the road of honest candor — all the way through this course. We could have overclaimed at every turn, crying "proven!" over each discovery, straining the gnat, promising far more than the evidence could hold. For a season, that would have felt stronger. But it would have left you with a faith that shatters at the very first hard question. Instead we conceded what was genuinely open, we refused what was merely assumed, and we stood immovably upon what is truly settled — and this is the settled thing: God has spoken, God has preserved His Word, and that Word is worthy of your absolute trust. Because we did not overclaim, nothing here will crumble when a skeptic presses hard, or a single dig is disputed. You may stake your very life upon this book — and your death as well. You may preach it without flinching, obey it without hedging, and rest your soul upon it in the darkest night. That is the fruit of honest confidence: not a nervous certainty that trembles before the next question, but a settled certainty that has already faced the questions, and stands.
blocks.es_reference: Ve ahora por qué tomamos el camino más difícil — el camino de la franqueza honesta — a lo largo de todo este curso. Pudimos haber exagerado en cada paso, clamando "¡probado!" sobre cada descubrimiento, colando el mosquito, prometiendo mucho más de lo que la evidencia podía sostener. Por una temporada, eso habría parecido más fuerte. Pero te habría dejado con una fe que se hace pedazos ante la primerísima pregunta difícil. En cambio concedimos lo genuinamente abierto, rechazamos lo meramente supuesto, y nos mantuvimos inconmovibles sobre lo verdaderamente establecido — y esto es lo establecido: Dios ha hablado, Dios ha preservado su Palabra, y esa Palabra es digna de tu confianza absoluta. Porque no exageramos, nada aquí se derrumbará cuando un escéptico presione con fuerza, o una sola excavación se dispute. Puedes apostar tu propia vida sobre este libro — y tu muerte también. Puedes predicarlo sin vacilar, obedecerlo sin rodeos, y descansar tu alma sobre él en la noche más oscura. Ese es el fruto de la confianza honesta: no una certeza nerviosa que tiembla ante la próxima pregunta, sino una certeza asentada que ya ha enfrentado las preguntas, y se mantiene.

blocks.en: 8. The Certainty Is Yours: A Sending
blocks.es_reference: 8. La Certeza Es Tuya: Un Envío

blocks.en: And so this course comes at last to its end, and it brings you back to the place where the whole journey began — with a Bible in your hands and a question in your heart: can I truly trust this? Now you have examined it, exactly as the Scripture itself commands you to do: "Prove all things; hold fast that which is good" (1 Thessalonians 5:21). You have proved it — the books, the words, the events, the land — and you have found it good, and true, and faithfully kept, and clothed with the authority of God. So now, do the other half: hold fast. Hold fast to the sure Word of God. Do not hold it timidly, like one clutching a treasure he half suspects is false; hold it boldly, like one who has weighed it in the balance and found it worthy. The certainty that Luke wrote to give Theophilus is now yours to keep — and yours to give away. So go: go and trust this Word; go and obey it; go and proclaim it to every soul who asks whether the Bible can be trusted. And you may tell them, on the evidence and on the sure promise of God: Yes. We can trust the Bible we hold.
blocks.es_reference: Y así este curso llega por fin a su final, y te trae de vuelta al lugar donde todo el viaje comenzó — con una Biblia en tus manos y una pregunta en tu corazón: ¿puedo realmente confiar en esto? Ahora lo has examinado, exactamente como la Escritura misma te manda hacer: "Examinadlo todo; retened lo bueno" (1 Tesalonicenses 5:21). Lo has examinado — los libros, las palabras, los eventos, la tierra — y lo has hallado bueno, y verdadero, y fielmente guardado, y revestido de la autoridad de Dios. Así que ahora, haz la otra mitad: retén firmemente. Retén firmemente la segura Palabra de Dios. No la retengas con timidez, como quien aferra un tesoro que a medias sospecha falso; retenla con audacia, como quien la ha pesado en la balanza y la ha hallado digna. La certeza que Lucas escribió para dar a Teófilo es ahora tuya para guardar — y tuya para regalar. Así que ve: ve y confía en esta Palabra; ve y obedécela; ve y proclámala a toda alma que pregunte si la Biblia puede ser confiada. Y puedes decirles, sobre la evidencia y sobre la segura promesa de Dios: Sí. Podemos confiar en la Biblia que tenemos.

sa.prompt: Name the four witnesses of the course and what each established.
sa.model: The first witness, the canon, gave us the right books, recognized and not invented. The second, the text, gave us the right words, preserved in abundance. The third, archaeology, showed the real events, the world of the Bible grounded in real soil. The fourth, geography, showed the real stage, a land so exactly known one can walk the Bible with a map. Together they establish that the Bible is a true and faithfully kept record.

sa.prompt: Explain how a cumulative case gains its force, using the unit's image.
sa.model: No single witness proves the Bible — correlation, not proof — but witnesses testify together, and their agreement has a force no one has alone. In a court, a single thread can be explained away, but a hundred threads braided together make a rope that holds. So the right books, the faithful words, the real events, and the real stage are each a strand, but together they make an overwhelming case. The cumulative weight is far greater than the sum of the parts.

sa.prompt: What is the purpose Luke states in Luke 1:1-4, and how does the course fulfill it?
sa.model: Luke tells Theophilus that many had written, that he had carefully investigated everything from the first following eyewitnesses, and had set it in orderly account — so that Theophilus would know the certainty of the things he was taught. The key word is certainty. Luke wrote not for a comforting feeling but for certainty. The course fulfills the same purpose: having examined the books, words, events, and land, it can tell every believer, you may know the certainty.

sa.prompt: Does the believer's certainty rest on the cumulative evidence? Explain the unit's answer.
sa.model: No — the evidence is the servant, not the master. If certainty rested on archaeology it would rise and fall with the next dig; what can be argued up can be argued down. The true ground of certainty is that God breathed out the Scripture and His Spirit bears witness that this is His Word. The evidence does not create that certainty; it clears away obstacles, confirms it, and silences the charge that faith is blind. Evidence serves faith; it is not its foundation.

sa.prompt: What is the headline the whole course moves toward, and what does it NOT claim?
sa.model: The headline is the absolute authority of the Word in your hands. It does not claim that you must first prove every word before you may trust it, and it does not rest that authority on the lost original manuscripts. It claims that because God gave and preserved His Word, His authority travels down through faithful copying and translation into the Bible you hold. The Word is not a fortress to defend inch by inch but a throne from which God speaks.

sa.prompt: Speak to the man in the pew: what does he hold, and what is the honest promise?
sa.model: He does not hold the original that Moses or Paul wrote; no one does. He holds a translation, an NKJV or a Reina-Valera, of a copy of a copy, and the course is honest about that. But God did not promise to hand him the autograph; He promised to preserve His Word — and He has done so faithfully and abundantly, so that the Bible open before him is the preserved, authoritative Word of God. He should read it, believe it, and obey it as such.

sa.prompt: Why did the course take the harder road of honest candor, and what is its fruit?
sa.model: The course could have overclaimed, crying 'proven!' at every turn and straining the gnat, and it would have felt stronger for a season — but it would have left a faith that shatters at the first hard question. Instead it conceded what was genuinely open, refused what was merely assumed, and stood on what is settled: God has spoken and preserved His Word, worthy of absolute trust. The fruit is not a nervous certainty that fears the next question, but a settled certainty that has faced the questions and stands.

sa.prompt: On what does the unit ultimately rest the Bible's absolute authority?
sa.model: Not on the believer first proving every word, and not on the lost original manuscripts alone, but on the fact that God gave His Word and God has preserved it. Because of this, His authority travels down through faithful copying and translation into the very Bible in the believer's hands. The apostles themselves preached from copies and translations with the full authority of God, and so may we. The Word is a throne from which God still speaks, with full authority, today.

sa.prompt: State the course's closing command and the final answer to the driving question.
sa.model: The closing command, from 1 Thessalonians 5:21, is: Prove all things; hold fast that which is good. Having proved the Bible — the books, the words, the events, the land — and found it good and true and kept, the believer is to hold it fast, not timidly but boldly. And the final answer to the question with which the course began, can we trust the Bible we hold, is yes — on the evidence and on the promise of God.

sa.prompt: In your own words, summarize what this whole course has shown about whether the Bible we hold can be trusted.
sa.model: The course called four witnesses — the canon, the text, archaeology, and geography — and each testified honestly, conceding open questions and refusing overclaims, yet together building an overwhelming cumulative case that the Bible is a true and faithfully preserved record. But the real ground of certainty is that God spoke it and preserved it, so that His absolute authority travels into the translation in my hands. On the evidence and the promise of God, the Bible I hold can be trusted.
